payload.title: Greek Orthodox Wedding Requirements and Ceremony Explained
payload.excerpt: A Greek Orthodox wedding is a sacrament, not a ceremony you write yourselves.
key_takeaways: Who can marry in the Church depends on its rules where you marry, so confirm eligibility with your parish priest before you book anything.
In Australia, the Archdiocese closes some dates and seasons to weddings, including the weeks before Christmas, Great Lent until Easter Sunday and the first half of August.
Church paperwork and civil paperwork are two separate tracks, and a wedding in Greece means checking with the local Metropolis, the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens.
The Archdiocese describes the crowning with the stefana as the climax of the service, and without the rings and the crowns the wedding cannot begin.

faq.q: Can a non-Orthodox partner marry in a Greek Orthodox church?
faq.a: Under the Archdiocese of Australia's rules, yes, if they are a baptised Christian of a denomination the Church accepts, such as Roman Catholic, Anglican, Uniting, Lutheran or Presbyterian. A non-Christian partner can marry in the Church only after baptism in an accepted denomination. Raise your partner's denomination at your first meeting with the priest.

faq.q: What documents do we need for a Greek Orthodox wedding?
faq.a: In Australia, the Archdiocese asks for a birth certificate or passport and a baptismal certificate for each of you, plus a Certificate of Celibacy for an Orthodox partner never married before. Divorced or widowed partners need extra papers. The Notice of Intended Marriage and the Application to the Archdiocese are completed with the priest at least a month ahead.

faq.q: Who can be a koumbaros or koumbara?
faq.a: Usually an Orthodox Christian. Under the Archdiocese's rules, a non-Orthodox Christian of an acceptable denomination may stand as sponsor at the wedding, but cannot become godparent to your children.

faq.q: Are there vows in a Greek Orthodox wedding?
faq.a: No. The Orthodox sacrament contains no vows or oaths. The blessing of the rings, the crowning and the common cup carry the meaning.

faq.q: How long is a Greek Orthodox wedding?
faq.a: There is no fixed length, so ask your priest for your church's running time. The Archdiocese asks the groom to arrive at least 15 minutes early and the bride's party at least five minutes early.

faq.q: Can a Greek Orthodox wedding be held outside a church?
faq.a: Plan on a church or chapel. The Archdiocese of Australia describes the rite taking place in church, before the Holy Altar. If you have a beach or garden in mind, raise it with your priest first. In Greece, several resorts have their own Orthodox chapel on the grounds, such as Nana Princess in Crete. Confirm any chapel with your priest and the Metropolis.

faq.q: Can we have a Greek Orthodox wedding in Greece if we live in Australia?
faq.a: Yes. Start with your parish priest, then confirm the Church's requirements with the local Metropolis. For the civil side, check with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees.
